metadata.title: Regret Analysis of Stochastic and Nonstochastic Multi-armed Bandit Problems

nodes.name: Stochastic multi-armed bandit problem
nodes.statement: Each arm $i \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ has unknown distribution $\nu_i$ on $[0,1]$; at each round $t$ the forecaster chooses $I_t$ and receives $X_{I_t,t} \sim \nu_{I_t}$. Goal: minimize pseudo-regret $\overline{R}_n = n\mu^* - \sum_{t=1}^n \E[\mu_{I_t}]$.

nodes.name: Adversarial multi-armed bandit problem
nodes.statement: At each round the forecaster picks $I_t \in \{1,\dots,K\}$ and the adversary picks gains $g_t \in [0,1]^K$; only $g_{I_t,t}$ is observed. Goal: minimize $R_n = \max_i \sum_t g_{i,t} - \sum_t g_{I_t,t}$ for any opponent.

nodes.name: Regret of a forecaster
nodes.statement: $R_n = \max_{i=1,\dots,K} \sum_{t=1}^n X_{i,t} - \sum_{t=1}^n X_{I_t,t}$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret
nodes.statement: $\overline{R}_n = \max_{i=1,\dots,K} \E\bigl[\sum_{t=1}^n X_{i,t} - \sum_{t=1}^n X_{I_t,t}\bigr]$.

nodes.name: Sub-Gaussian-type moment condition
nodes.statement: There exists a convex function $\psi$ on $\R$ such that for all $\lambda \ge 0$, $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda(X-\E[X])} \le \psi(\lambda)$ and $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda(\E[X]-X)} \le \psi(\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Legendre-Fenchel transform of $\psi$
nodes.statement: $\psi^*(\epsilon) = \sup_{\lambda \in \R}\bigl(\lambda \epsilon - \psi(\lambda)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Hoeffding's lemma (cited)
nodes.statement: If $X \in [0,1]$ then $\ln \E\,e^{\lambda(X-\E X)} \le \lambda^2/8$.

nodes.name: $\psi$-concentration of sample mean
nodes.statement: $\P(\mu_i - \widehat{\mu}_{i,s} > \epsilon) \le e^{-s\,\psi^*(\epsilon)}$.

nodes.name: $(\alpha,\psi)$-UCB
nodes.statement: Optimism-in-face-of-uncertainty strategy that picks $I_t \in \arg\max_i [\widehat{\mu}_{i,T_i(t-1)} + (\psi^*)^{-1}(\alpha \ln t / T_i(t-1))]$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of $(\alpha,\psi)$-UCB
nodes.statement: Assume reward distributions satisfy the $\psi$-condition. With $\alpha > 2$, $(\alpha,\psi)$-UCB satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le \sum_{i:\Delta_i>0}\bigl(\frac{\alpha \Delta_i}{\psi^*(\Delta_i/2)} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha-2}\bigr)$.
assumptions: Reward distributions satisfy the moment condition (AssumP17.1)

nodes.name: Bounded-rewards UCB regret bound
nodes.statement: For $X \in [0,1]$ and $\alpha$-UCB, $\overline{R}_n \le \sum_{i:\Delta_i>0}\bigl(\frac{2\alpha}{\Delta_i}\ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha-2}\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP17.1 (UCB regret)
nodes.statement: If $I_t = i$, at least one of the events (UCB1)-(UCB3) holds; bound the probability of (UCB1) and (UCB2) via union bound and $\psi$-concentration; (UCB3) gives the deterministic-count term.

nodes.name: Set up the three failure events
nodes.statement: If $I_t = i$ then at least one of (UCB1) $\widehat{\mu}_{i^*,T_{i^*}(t-1)} + (\psi^*)^{-1}(\alpha \ln t/T_{i^*}(t-1)) \le \mu^*$, (UCB2) $\widehat{\mu}_{i,T_i(t-1)} > \mu_i + (\psi^*)^{-1}(\alpha \ln t/T_i(t-1))$, (UCB3) $T_i(t-1) < \alpha \ln n / \psi^*(\Delta_i/2)$ must hold.

nodes.name: Decompose $\E\,T_i(n)$
nodes.statement: Let $u = \lceil \alpha \ln n / \psi^*(\Delta_i/2) \rceil$; then $\E\,T_i(n) \le u + \sum_{t=u+1}^n \P((\text{UCB1) or (UCB2) is true})$.

nodes.name: Bound (UCB1) probability via union bound and concentration
nodes.statement: Apply union bound over $s \in \{1,\dots,t\}$ and equation EP17.3: $\P((\text{UCB1) is true}) \le \sum_{s=1}^t t^{-\alpha} = t^{-(\alpha-1)}$.

nodes.name: Conclude by summing
nodes.statement: The same bound applies to (UCB2); summing gives $\E\,T_i(n) \le u + 2\sum_{t=u+1}^n t^{-(\alpha-1)}$, yielding the claim.

nodes.name: Lai-Robbins distribution-dependent lower bound
nodes.statement: For any consistent strategy ($\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ on Bernoulli arms with $\Delta_i > 0$), $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \overline{R}_n / \ln n \ge \sum_{i:\Delta_i>0} \Delta_i / \mathrm{kl}(\mu_i,\mu^*)$.
assumptions: $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any $a > 0$ and any suboptimal $i$

nodes.name: Pinsker / log-bound on Bernoulli KL
nodes.statement: $2(p-q)^2 \le \mathrm{kl}(p,q) \le (p-q)^2/(q(1-q))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP17.2 (LR85 lower bound)
nodes.statement: Three-step argument restricted to two arms: introduce a modified bandit where arm 2 becomes optimal, use change-of-measure with KL log-likelihood, and apply maximal SLLN to lower-bound $\E T_2(n)$.

nodes.name: Notation and modified bandit
nodes.statement: Pick $\mu_2' \in (\mu_1,1)$ such that $\mathrm{kl}(\mu_2,\mu_2') \le (1+\epsilon)\mathrm{kl}(\mu_2,\mu_1)$; define empirical log-likelihood $\widehat{\mathrm{kl}}_s$ and change-of-measure identity $\P'(A) = \E[\mathds{1}_A \exp(-\widehat{\mathrm{kl}}_{T_2(n)})]$.

nodes.name: Show $\P(C_n) = o(1)$
nodes.statement: Using the change-of-measure and Markov's inequality, $\P(C_n) \le n^{1-\epsilon/2}\,\E'[n - T_2(n)]/(n - f_n) = o(1)$ since arm 2 is optimal in the modified bandit.

nodes.name: Apply maximal SLLN to deduce $\P(T_2(n) < f_n) = o(1)$
nodes.statement: Maximal strong law of large numbers gives $\lim_n \P(\frac{\mathrm{kl}(\mu_2,\mu_2')}{(1-\epsilon)\ln n}\max_{s\le f_n}\widehat{\mathrm{kl}}_s \le \frac{1-\epsilon/2}{1-\epsilon}\mathrm{kl}(\mu_2,\mu_2')) = 1$, so $\P(T_2(n) < f_n) = o(1)$.

nodes.name: Conclude bound on $\E\,T_2(n)$
nodes.statement: Combining gives $\E\,T_2(n) \ge (1+o(1))\frac{1-\epsilon}{1+\epsilon}\ln n / \mathrm{kl}(\mu_2,\mu_1)$, which yields the claim by letting $\epsilon \to 0$.

nodes.name: Exp3 (Exponential weights for Exploration and Exploitation)
nodes.statement: Randomized forecaster that maintains $p_t$ via exponential weighting on importance-weighted loss estimates $\tilde{\ell}_{i,t} = \ell_{i,t}\,\mathds{1}_{I_t=i}/p_{i,t}$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of Exp3
nodes.statement: If $\eta = \sqrt{2\ln K/(nK)}$ then $\overline{R}_n \le \sqrt{2nK\ln K}$; with anytime schedule $\eta_t = \sqrt{\ln K/(tK)}$, $\overline{R}_n \le 2\sqrt{nK\ln K}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP17.3 (Exp3 pseudo-regret)
nodes.statement: Show $\overline{R}_n \le \frac{K}{2}\sum_t \eta_t + \ln K/\eta_n$ via cumulant-generating-function decomposition; specialize to the two learning-rate schedules.

nodes.name: Useful equalities for $\tilde{\ell}$
nodes.statement: Establish $\E_{i\sim p_t}\tilde{\ell}_{i,t} = \ell_{I_t,t}$, $\E_{I_t\sim p_t}\tilde{\ell}_{i,t} = \ell_{i,t}$, $\E_{i\sim p_t}\tilde{\ell}_{i,t}^2 = \ell_{I_t,t}^2/p_{I_t,t}$, $\E_{I_t\sim p_t}1/p_{I_t,t}=K$.

nodes.name: Bound first cumulant term
nodes.statement: Use $\ln x \le x-1$ and $\exp(-x)-1+x \le x^2/2$ for $x\ge 0$ to obtain $\ln \E_{i\sim p_t}\exp(-\eta_t(\tilde{\ell}_{i,t}-\E_{k\sim p_t}\tilde{\ell}_{k,t})) \le \eta_t^2/(2 p_{I_t,t})$.

nodes.name: Telescope second cumulant term
nodes.statement: With $\Phi_t(\eta) = \eta^{-1}\ln(K^{-1}\sum_i \exp(-\eta \tilde{L}_{i,t}))$, $-\eta_t^{-1}\ln \E_{i\sim p_t}\exp(-\eta_t \tilde{\ell}_{i,t}) = \Phi_{t-1}(\eta_t) - \Phi_t(\eta_t)$.

nodes.name: Sum over $t$ and apply Abel transform
nodes.statement: Combine the bounds, take expectations, and Abel-summing yields $\E[\sum_t g_{k,t} - \sum_t g_{I_t,t}] \le \frac{K}{2}\sum_t \eta_t + \ln K/\eta_n + \E\sum_{t<n}(\Phi_t(\eta_{t+1})-\Phi_t(\eta_t))$.

nodes.name: Show $\Phi_t'(\eta) \ge 0$ to drop telescoping term
nodes.statement: $\Phi_t'(\eta) = \eta^{-2}\,\K(p_t^\eta, p_1) \ge 0$, so for non-increasing $\eta_t$ the residual telescoping term is nonpositive, yielding the claimed bound.

nodes.name: Biased gain estimate concentration (for Exp3.P)
nodes.statement: For $\beta \le 1$ and $\tilde{g}_{i,t} = (g_{i,t}\mathds{1}_{I_t=i}+\beta)/p_{i,t}$, with probability at least $1-\delta$: $\sum_{t=1}^n g_{i,t} \le \sum_{t=1}^n \tilde{g}_{i,t} + \ln(1/\delta)/\beta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP17.2
nodes.statement: Bound the conditional MGF by $1$ using $\exp(x)\le 1+x+x^2$ for $x\le 1$, giving $\E\exp(\beta\sum_t g_{i,t} - \beta\sum_t \tilde{g}_{i,t}) \le 1$; apply Markov.

nodes.name: Exp3.P
nodes.statement: Mixed exponential-weight forecaster on biased gain estimates $\tilde{g}_{i,t} = (g_{i,t}\mathds{1}_{I_t=i}+\beta)/p_{i,t}$ with mixing distribution.

nodes.name: High-probability regret bound for Exp3.P
nodes.statement: With suitable $\beta,\eta,\gamma$, with probability $\ge 1-\delta$, $R_n \le 5.15\sqrt{nK\ln(K\delta^{-1})}$; alternative tuning yields $R_n \le \sqrt{nK/\ln K}\,\ln(\delta^{-1}) + 5.15\sqrt{nK\ln K}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP17.4 (Exp3.P high-prob bound)
nodes.statement: Three-step argument: derive $R_n \le \beta nK + \gamma n + (1+\beta)\eta K n + \ln(K\delta^{-1})/\beta + \ln K/\eta$ via cumulant analysis with mixing; substitute the parameter choices.

nodes.name: Notations and simple equalities (mixing)
nodes.statement: Decompose $-\E_{i\sim p_t}\tilde{g}_{i,t}$ via the no-mixing distribution $w_t = (p_t-u)/(1-\gamma)$ and a cumulant-generating identity.

nodes.name: Bound first cumulant under mixing
nodes.statement: Use $\eta\tilde{g}_{i,t} \le 1$ (since $(1+\beta)\eta K \le \gamma$) to get $\ln \E_{i\sim w_t}\exp(\eta(\tilde{g}_{i,t}-\E_{k\sim p_t}\tilde{g}_{k,t})) \le \frac{1+\beta}{1-\gamma}\eta^2 \sum_i \tilde{g}_{i,t}$.

nodes.name: Sum and apply Lemma LP17.2
nodes.statement: Sum the previous bound and apply Lemma LP17.2 with a union bound to obtain $R_n \le \beta nK + \gamma n + (1+\beta)\eta K n + \ln(K\delta^{-1})/\beta + \ln K/\eta$.

nodes.name: Plug in tuning to get the two bounds
nodes.statement: Substitute $\beta = \sqrt{\ln(K\delta^{-1})/(nK)}$, $\eta = 0.95\sqrt{\ln K/(nK)}$, $\gamma = 1.05\sqrt{K\ln K/n}$; check $(1+\beta)\eta K \le \gamma \le 1/2$; same for the second tuning.

nodes.name: Expected regret of Exp3.P
nodes.statement: With the appropriate tuning, $\E\,R_n \le 5.15\sqrt{nK\ln K} + \sqrt{nK/\ln K}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.5 by integrating high-prob bound
nodes.statement: Integrate the deviation inequality $\P(W > \ln(1/\delta))$ via $\E W \le \int_0^1 \delta^{-1}\P(W>\ln(1/\delta))d\delta$ applied to the relevant rescaled regret.

nodes.name: Minimax lower bound for adversarial bandits
nodes.statement: $\inf \sup (\max_i \E\sum_t Y_{i,t} - \E\sum_t Y_{I_t,t}) \ge \frac{1}{20}\sqrt{nK}$ where the supremum is over Bernoulli reward distributions and the infimum over forecasters.

nodes.name: Stochastic-adversary lower bound lemma
nodes.statement: For $\epsilon \in [0,1)$, $\max_i \E_i \sum_t (Y_{i,t}-Y_{I_t,t}) \ge n\epsilon(1 - 1/K - \sqrt{\epsilon \ln \frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}}\sqrt{n/(2K)})$ where $\E_i$ is the expectation against the bandit with arm $i$ optimal (parameter $(1+\epsilon)/2$).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma LP17.3 (5-step)
nodes.statement: Lower-bound the average regret over $K$ bandits via empirical play distribution, Pinsker's inequality, KL chain rule, concavity of $\sqrt{\cdot}$, and Fubini for randomized forecasters.

nodes.name: Empirical distribution of plays
nodes.statement: For deterministic forecasters with $J_n \sim q_n$, derive $\frac{1}{K}\sum_i \E_i\sum_t(Y_{i,t}-Y_{I_t,t}) = \epsilon n(1 - \frac{1}{K}\sum_i \P_i(J_n=i))$.

nodes.name: Apply Pinsker's inequality
nodes.statement: $\P_i(J_n=i) \le \P_0(J_n=i) + \sqrt{\K(\P_0,\P_i)/2}$ gives $\frac{1}{K}\sum_i\P_i(J_n=i) \le 1/K + \frac{1}{K}\sum_i \sqrt{\K(\P_0,\P_i)/2}$.

nodes.name: Compute KL via chain rule
nodes.statement: Iteratively apply chain rule to get $\K(\P_0^n,\P_i^n) = \K((1-\epsilon)/2, (1+\epsilon)/2)\,\E_0\,T_i(n)$.

nodes.name: Conclude for deterministic forecasters via concavity
nodes.statement: By concavity of $\sqrt{\cdot}$, $\frac{1}{K}\sum_i \sqrt{\K(\P_0,\P_i)} \le \sqrt{\frac{n}{K}\,\K((1-\epsilon)/2,(1+\epsilon)/2)}$, then combine with previous steps.

nodes.name: Extend to randomized forecasters via Fubini
nodes.statement: Fubini's theorem reduces the randomized case to applying the deterministic bound conditional on each realization of the forecaster's random bits.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP17.6 (minimax lower bound)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP17.3 with $\epsilon$ optimized of order $\sqrt{K/n}$.

nodes.name: $\cS$-Exp3 (per-context Exp3)
nodes.statement: Run a separate instance of Exp3 for each distinct context $s \in \cS$.
output: Arm choice $I_t$ for each round given context $s_t$

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of $\cS$-Exp3 with side information
nodes.statement: There exists a randomized forecaster ($\cS$-Exp3) with $\overline{R}^{\cS}_n \le \sqrt{2n|\cS|K\ln K}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.7
nodes.statement: Decompose the regret per context, apply Theorem TP17.3 to each per-context Exp3 instance, then use Jensen's inequality and $\sum_s n_s = n$.

nodes.name: Exp4 (Exponential weights with Experts)
nodes.statement: Maintain a distribution $q_t$ over $N$ experts; sample arm from $p_t$ where $p_{i,t} = \E_{j\sim q_t} \xi_{i,t}^j$; update $q_t$ via exponential weights on estimated expert losses $\tilde{y}_{j,t} = \E_{i\sim \xi_t^j}\tilde{\ell}_{i,t}$.
input: Number of arms $K$, number of experts $N$, learning rates $(\eta_t)$

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of Exp4
nodes.statement: With $\eta = \sqrt{2\ln N/(nK)}$, $\overline{R}^{\mathrm{ctx}}_n \le \sqrt{2nN\ln K}$ (paper writes $\sqrt{2nN\ln K}$, but the standard tight bound is $\sqrt{2nK\ln N}$); anytime: $\overline{R}^{\mathrm{ctx}}_n \le 2\sqrt{nN\ln K}$.
assumptions: $N$ randomized experts producing distributions $\xi_t^j$ over arms

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.8 (Exp4 pseudo-regret)
nodes.statement: Apply the Exp3 analysis to a forecaster over $N$ experts using $\tilde{y}_{j,t}$, exploit unbiasedness equalities, and bound the second-moment term using Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Exp3 with rebellious play distribution
nodes.statement: If $I_t \sim q_t$ (arbitrary, with $q_{t,i} \ge \epsilon > 0$) instead of $p_t$, Exp3 satisfies $\max_k \E_{I^n\sim q^n}[\sum_t \E_{i\sim p_t}\ell_{i,t} - \sum_t \ell_{k,t}] \le \sqrt{2n\ln K/\epsilon}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.9 (Exp3 with rebellious play)
nodes.statement: Adapt the Exp3 cumulant analysis with the play distribution $q_t$ in the loss estimate; bound $\E_{I_t\sim q_t}[p_{I_t,t}/q_{I_t,t}^2] \le 1/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of Exp4 with mixing
nodes.statement: Exp4 with mixing coefficient $\gamma$ and $\eta = \gamma/K$ satisfies $\overline{R}^{\mathrm{ctx}}_n \le \gamma n/2 + K\ln N/\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.10
nodes.statement: Mirror the original Exp4 proof with the negative-exponential bound $\exp(-x) \le 1-x+x^2/2$; the term $\frac{\gamma}{K}\sum_t\sum_i\ell_{i,t}$ is upper-bounded by $\gamma n$.

nodes.name: Best-context-set regret bound (Exp4-over-$\cS$-Exp3)
nodes.statement: There exists a forecaster achieving $\overline{R}^{\Theta}_n = \mathcal{O}(n^{2/3}(\max_\theta |\cS_\theta|K\ln K)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|})$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.11
nodes.statement: Run Exp4 with mixing $\gamma$ over $|\Theta|$ instances of $\cS$-Exp3 as experts; combine TP17.10 and TP17.9 (with $\epsilon = \gamma/K$); optimize $\gamma$ of order $n^{-1/3}(\max_\theta|\cS_\theta|K\ln K)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|}$.

nodes.name: VE (VC dimension by Exponentiation)
nodes.statement: First $n'$ rounds: choose arms uniformly; build $\cF' \subseteq \cF$ minimal w.r.t.\ first $n'$ contexts; for $t > n'$ run Exp4.P treating policies in $\cF'$ as experts.
input: Policy class $\cF$ of binary policies of VC-dim $d$

nodes.name: Regret of VE on stochastic contextual bandits
nodes.statement: For any binary policy class $\cF$ of VC-dim $d$ and $n>d$, with $n' = \sqrt{n(2d\ln(en/d) + \ln(3/\delta))}$, $\sum_t \ell_{I_t,t} - n\inf_{f\in\cF}\ell_D(f) \le c\sqrt{n(d\ln(en/d)+\ln(3/\delta))}$ w.p. $\ge 1-\delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.12 (VE regret)
nodes.statement: Decompose the regret using a witness $f' \in \cF'$ that agrees with $f^*$ on the first $n'$ points; bound the disagreement on remaining points via Sauer-Shelah and a permutation argument; control $\sum_t \ell_{f^*(x_t),t}$ via Chernoff bounds.

nodes.name: Bound exploration cost and apply Exp4.P
nodes.statement: $\sum_t \ell_{I_t,t} \le n' + \sum_{t>n'}\ell_{f'(x_t),t} + c\sqrt{2(n-n')\ln(3|\cF'|/\delta)}$ via uniform exploration on first $n'$ rounds and Exp4.P bound after.

nodes.name: Apply Sauer-Shelah
nodes.statement: By Sauer-Shelah, $|\cF'| \le (en/d)^d$, giving $c\sqrt{2n(d\ln(en/d)+\ln(3/\delta))}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff bound for $\sum_t \ell_{f^*(x_t),t}$
nodes.statement: $\P(\sum_{t>n'}\ell_{f^*(x_t),t} > (n-n')\ell_D(f^*) + \sqrt{(n-n')\ln(3/\delta)/2}) \le \delta$.

nodes.name: Permutation argument bounds $\sum_t \mathds{1}_{f'(x_t)\neq f^*(x_t)}$
nodes.statement: Use random permutation $\sigma$ and Sauer-Shelah to get $\sum_{t>n'} \mathds{1}_{f'(x_{\sigma(t)})\neq f^*(x_{\sigma(t)})} \le (n/n')(2d\ln(en/d)+\ln(3/\delta))$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Optimize $n'$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Substitute $n' = \sqrt{n(2d\ln(en/d) + \ln(3/\delta))}$ to balance terms.

nodes.name: Banditron
nodes.statement: Bandit variant of multiclass Perceptron: predict $\hat{y}_t = \arg\max_i (W_t x_t)_i$, sample $Y_t \sim p_t$ with $p_{i,t} = (1-\gamma)\mathds{1}_{\hat{y}_t=i} + \gamma/K$; update $W_{t+1} = W_t + \tilde{X}_t$ with importance-weighted matrix update.
output: Sequence of predictions $Y_t$ and weight matrices $W_t$

nodes.name: Proof of Banditron mistake bound TP17.13
nodes.statement: Bound first and second moments of $\tilde{X}_t$, derive $\E\|W_{n+1}\|^2 \le (2K/\gamma)\sum_t \P(y_t\neq \hat{y}_t) + 2\gamma n$, combine with Cauchy-Schwarz upper bound and Perceptron-style lower bound on $\langle U, W_{n+1}\rangle$.

nodes.name: Compute conditional moments of $\tilde{X}_t$
nodes.statement: $\E_t[(\tilde{X}_t)_{i,j}] = (X_t)_{i,j}$ and $\E_t\|\tilde{X}_t\|^2 \le 2((K/\gamma)\mathds{1}_{y_t\neq\hat{y}_t} + \gamma\mathds{1}_{y_t=\hat{y}_t})$.

nodes.name: Upper bound $\E\langle U, W_{n+1}\rangle$
nodes.statement: Cauchy-Schwarz and Jensen give $\E\langle U, W_{n+1}\rangle \le \|U\|\sqrt{(2K/\gamma)\sum_t \P(y_t\neq\hat{y}_t) + 2\gamma n}$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\E\langle U, W_{n+1}\rangle$ via hinge loss
nodes.statement: $\E\langle U, W_{n+1}\rangle \ge \sum_t \P(y_t\neq\hat{y}_t) - L_n(U)$ using $\ell_t(U) \ge \mathds{1}_{y_t\neq\hat{y}_t} - \langle U, X_t\rangle$.

nodes.name: Solve quadratic and tune $\gamma$
nodes.statement:
Combine upper and lower bounds, solve for $\sum_t \P(y_t
eq \hat{y}_t)$, account for $\P(y_t
eq Y_t) = (1-\gamma)\P(y_t
eq\hat{y}_t) + \gamma$, and set $\gamma = (K/n)^{1/3}$.

nodes.name: Online linear optimization with bandit feedback
nodes.statement: At each round, forecaster picks $x_t \in \cK \subseteq \R^d$ (compact convex), adversary picks $\ell_t \in \cL \subseteq \R^d$; feedback is the scalar $x_t^\top \ell_t$. Goal: minimize $\overline{R}_n = \E\sum_t x_t^\top \ell_t - \min_{x\in\cK}\E\sum_t x^\top \ell_t$.

nodes.name: John's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: If the minimal-volume ellipsoid $\cE$ of a convex set $\cK \subset \R^d$ is the unit ball of an inner product, then there exist $M \le d(d+1)/2 + 1$ contact points $u_1,\dots,u_M$ between $\cE$ and $\cK$ and a probability distribution $(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_M)$ such that $x = d\sum_i \mu_i \langle x,u_i\rangle u_i$ for all $x \in \R^d$.
assumptions: the minimal-volume enclosing ellipsoid is the unit ball of an inner product
conclusions: Existence of $M \le d(d+1)/2+1$ contact points and a probability distribution implementing the resolution-of-identity formula

nodes.name: Exp2 with John's exploration
nodes.statement: Variant of Exp3 over a finite arm set $\cK$ using estimated linear losses $\langle x,\tilde{\ell}_t\rangle$ and exploration distribution $\mu$ supported on John's contact points.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of Exp2 with John's exploration
nodes.statement: For $\eta d \le \gamma$, Exp2 with John's exploration satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le 2\gamma n + \ln N/\eta + \eta n d$. With $\eta = \sqrt{\ln N/(3nd)}$ and $\gamma = \eta d$, $\overline{R}_n \le 2\sqrt{3nd\ln N}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.15
nodes.statement: Adapt Exp3 analysis to include exploration; bound $\sum_x p_t(x)\langle x,\tilde{\ell}_t\rangle^2 \le \langle P_t^{-1}x_t, x_t\rangle$, take expectation to get $d$ via spectral decomposition; use $P_t \succeq (\gamma/d)I$ from John's theorem.

nodes.name: Subdifferentiable function
nodes.statement: $f:\cX\to\R$ is subdifferentiable if for all $x \in \cX$ there exists $g \in \R^d$ such that $f(x)-f(y) \le g^\top(x-y)$ for all $y \in \cX$. Such a $g$ is called a subgradient of $f$ at $x$.

nodes.name: Legendre-Fenchel transform of $f$
nodes.statement: $f^*(u) = \sup_{x\in\cX}(x^\top u - f(x))$.

nodes.name: Legendre function
nodes.statement: Continuous $F:\overline{\cD}\to\R$ with $\cD$ open convex is Legendre if (i) $F$ is strictly convex with continuous first partials on $\cD$ and (ii) $\lim_{x\to \overline{\cD}\setminus\cD}\|\nabla F(x)\| = +\infty$.

nodes.name: Bregman divergence
nodes.statement: $D_F(x,y) = F(x) - F(y) - (x-y)^\top \nabla F(y)$ for a Legendre function $F$.

nodes.name: Legendre duality / dual Bregman identity (cited)
nodes.statement:
$F^{**} = F$, $
abla F^* = (
abla F)^{-1}$ on $\cD^*$, and $D_F(x,y) = D_{F^*}(
abla F(y),
abla F(x))$.

nodes.name: Generalized Pythagorean inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: Let $\cK \subseteq \overline{\cD}$ closed convex with $\cK \cap \cD \neq \emptyset$. The Bregman projection $z = \arg\min_{y\in\cK} D_F(y,x)$ exists and is unique; for $z \in \cK\cap\cD$ and $y \in \cK$, $D_F(y,x) \ge D_F(y,z) + D_F(z,x)$.

nodes.name: OMD (Online Mirror Descent)
nodes.statement:
At each round play $x_t$ and observe $\ell_t$; dual update $w_{t+1} = 
abla F^*(
abla F(x_t) - \eta
abla \ell_t(x_t))$; primal Bregman projection $x_{t+1} = \arg\min_{y\in\cK} D_F(y,w_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Regret of OMD (Legendre $F$)
nodes.statement:
Under the consistency condition $
abla F(x) - \eta
abla\ell(x) \in \cD^*$, OMD satisfies $\sum_t (\ell_t(x_t)-\ell_t(x)) \le (F(x)-F(x_1))/\eta + \eta^{-1}\sum_t D_{F^*}(
abla F(x_t)-\eta
abla\ell_t(x_t),
abla F(x_t))$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.16
nodes.statement: Use subdifferentiability and the three-point identity for Bregman divergence; apply Lemma LP17.5 to drop the projection-cost term; sum and use $D_F(x,x_1) \le F(x)-F(x_1)$.

nodes.name: Regret of OMD with non-Legendre $F$
nodes.statement: If $F$ has effective domain $\cK$ and $F^*$ is differentiable on $\R^d$, then $\sum_t (\ell_t(x_t)-\ell_t(x)) \le (F(x)-F(x_1))/\eta + \eta^{-1}\sum_t D_{F^*}(-\eta\sum_{s\le t}\nabla\ell_s(x_s), -\eta\sum_{s< t}\nabla\ell_s(x_s))$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.17
nodes.statement: Use subdifferentiability and Fenchel-Young, observe $F^*(0)=-F(x_1)$, telescope the sum to expose Bregman terms in the dual.

nodes.name: OSMD (Online Stochastic Mirror Descent)
nodes.statement: Replace the gradient in OMD with a random unbiased estimate $\tilde{g}_t$ of $\nabla\ell_t(x_t)$, computed from a perturbation $\tilde{x}_t$ of $x_t$ where $\ell_t$ is queried.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of OSMD
nodes.statement:
Under consistency and $\E[	ilde{g}_t \mid x_t] = 
abla\ell_t(x_t)$, $\overline{R}_n \le (\sup_x F(x) - F(x_1))/\eta + \eta^{-1}\sum_t \E\,D_{F^*}(
abla F(x_t)-\eta	ilde{g}_t,
abla F(x_t)) + \sum_t \E[\|x_t-	ilde{x}_t\|\,\|	ilde{g}_t\|_*]$; for linear losses $\|x_t-	ilde{x}_t\|$ may be replaced by $\|x_t-\E[	ilde{x}_t\mid x_t]\|$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.18
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem TP17.16 to $\tilde{g}_t$, use unbiasedness to recover the gradient inequality, and absorb the perturbation gap via $\|x_t-\tilde{x}_t\|\,\|\tilde{g}_t\|_*$.

nodes.name: Online combinatorial optimization (semi-bandit)
nodes.statement: $\cC \subseteq \{0,1\}^d$ with $\|v\|_1 = m$ for $v\in\cC$, linear losses $\ell_t \in [0,1]^d$; semi-bandit feedback reveals $(\ell_t(i)v_t(i))_i$. Goal: bound $\overline{R}_n$.

nodes.name: Semi-bandit unbiased loss estimate
nodes.statement: $\tilde{\ell}_t(i) = \ell_t(i)v_t(i)/x_t(i)$ for $i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$.

nodes.name: OSMD with negative entropy on semi-bandit
nodes.statement: With $F(x) = \sum_i x_i\ln x_i - \sum_i x_i$ on $\cK = \mathrm{conv}(\cC)$, OSMD satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le (m/\eta)\ln(d/m) + (\eta/2)\sum_t \sum_i \E[x_t(i)\tilde{\ell}_t(i)^2]$. With the semi-bandit estimate and $\eta = \sqrt{(2m/(nd))\ln(d/m)}$, $\overline{R}_n \le \sqrt{2mdn\ln(d/m)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.19
nodes.statement: Bound $F(x)-F(x_1) \le m\ln(d/m)$ using Jensen; use $\Theta(x) = \exp(x)-1-x \le x^2/2$ for $x \le 0$ on $D_{F^*}$; bound $x_t(i)\E[\tilde{\ell}_t(i)^2] \le 1$.

nodes.name: $\omega$-potential
nodes.statement: A convex, continuously differentiable $\psi:(-\infty,a)\to\R^*_+$ is an $\omega$-potential if $\lim_{x\to-\infty}\psi(x)=\omega$, $\lim_{x\to a}\psi(x)=+\infty$, $\psi'>0$, and $\int_\omega^{\omega+1}|\psi^{-1}(s)|ds < +\infty$. Set $F_\psi(x) = \sum_i \int_\omega^{x_i}\psi^{-1}(s)ds$ on $\cD = (\omega,+\infty)^d$.

nodes.name: Properties of $F_\psi$ for $0$-potentials
nodes.statement: For a $0$-potential $\psi$, $F_\psi$ is Legendre and for $u \le v$ componentwise, $D_{F^*}(u,v) \le \frac{1}{2}\sum_i \psi'(v_i)(u_i-v_i)^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP17.6
nodes.statement: Verify Legendre property, compute $\nabla F^*(u) = (\psi(u_1),\dots,\psi(u_d))$, Taylor-expand $D_{F^*}$ and use convexity of $\psi$ to bound $\max_{s\in[u_i,v_i]}\psi'(s)\le\psi'(v_i)$.

nodes.name: OSMD with $0$-potential
nodes.statement: $\overline{R}_n \le (\sup F_\psi - F_\psi(x_1))/\eta + (\eta/2)\sum_t \sum_i \E[\tilde{\ell}_t(i)^2/(\psi^{-1})'(x_t(i))]$. With $\psi(x)=(-x)^{-q}$ and the semi-bandit estimate, $\overline{R}_n \le q\sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1}mdn}$, in particular $\overline{R}_n \le 2\sqrt{2mdn}$ for $q=2$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.20
nodes.statement: First inequality follows from the semi-bandit OSMD bound and Lemma LP17.6 with $\psi'(\psi^{-1}(s)) = 1/(\psi^{-1})'(s)$. For $\psi(x)=(-x)^{-q}$ apply Holder's inequality and explicit calculation.

nodes.name: Ball-bandit unbiased loss estimate
nodes.section: 5.5 Improved bounds for the Euclidean ball
nodes.statement: $\tilde{\ell}_t = d(1-\xi_t)\frac{\tilde{x}_t^\top \ell_t}{1-\|x_t\|}\,\tilde{x}_t$, where $\xi_t\sim\mathrm{Ber}(\|x_t\|)$, $I_t \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\{1,\dots,d\})$, $\epsilon_t$ Rademacher, $\tilde{x}_t = x_t/\|x_t\|$ if $\xi_t=1$ else $\epsilon_t e_{I_t}$.

nodes.name: OSMD on the Euclidean ball
nodes.section: 5.5 Improved bounds for the Euclidean ball
nodes.statement: On $\cK = \{x: \|x\|\le 1\}$ with $F(x) = -\ln(1-\|x\|) - \|x\|$ on shrunk $\cK' = (1-\gamma)\cK$ and the ball loss estimate, for $\eta d \le 1/2$, $\overline{R}_n \le \gamma n + \ln(\gamma^{-1})/\eta + \eta\sum_t \E[(1-\|x_t\|)\|\tilde{\ell}_t\|^2]$. With $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{n}$, $\eta = \sqrt{\ln n/(2nd)}$, $\overline{R}_n \le 3\sqrt{dn\ln n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.21 (ball OSMD)
nodes.section: 5.5 Improved bounds for the Euclidean ball
nodes.statement: Show $F$ is Legendre on the open ball, $\cD^* = \R^d$, hence consistency holds. Compute closed-form $\nabla F^*$ and $D_{F^*}$; show $\Theta(u,v) \le \|u-v\|^2$ when $(\|u\|-\|v\|)/(1+\|v\|) \ge -1/2$ via $\ln(1+x)\ge x-x^2$ on $x\ge -1/2$; bound the variance term.

nodes.name: Nonlinear adversarial bandit (two-point feedback)
nodes.statement: Convex $G$-Lipschitz differentiable losses $\ell_t : \cK \to \R$; at each round the forecaster queries $\ell_t$ at two chosen points and plays one of them. Goal: bound $\overline{R}_n$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear adversarial bandit (one-point feedback)
nodes.statement: Convex $G$-Lipschitz differentiable losses uniformly bounded by $L$; only $\ell_t(\tilde{X}_t)$ at the played point is observed. Goal: bound $\overline{R}_n$.

nodes.name: OSGD (Online Stochastic Gradient Descent)
nodes.statement: OSMD with $F(x) = \frac{1}{2}\|x\|^2$: Euclidean projection of $x_t - \eta\,\tilde{g}_t(x_t)$ onto $\cK$ each round.

nodes.name: Two-point gradient estimate
nodes.statement: $\tilde{g}_t(x_t) = \frac{d}{2\delta}(\ell_t(X_t^+)-\ell_t(X_t^-))S$, with $X_t^\pm = x_t \pm \delta S$ and $S \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\Sphere)$.

nodes.name: One-point gradient estimate
nodes.statement: $\tilde{g}_t(x) = \frac{d}{\delta}\ell_t(x+\delta S)\,S$, $S \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\Sphere)$.

nodes.name: Divergence-theorem identity
nodes.statement: For differentiable $\ell:\R^d\to\R$, $\nabla\int_{\Ball}\ell(x+\delta b)\,db = \int_{\Sphere}\ell(x+\delta s)\,s\,d\sigma(s)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP17.7 via Divergence Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply the Divergence Theorem: $\nabla\int_\Ball \ell(x+\delta b)db = \int_\Ball \nabla\ell(x+\delta b)db = \int_\Sphere \frac{1}{\delta}\ell(x+\delta s)\,s\,d\sigma(s)$.

nodes.name: Smoothed-gradient identity (Stokes-style)
nodes.statement: For $B \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\Ball)$, $S \sim \mathrm{Unif}(\Sphere)$ and differentiable $\ell$, $\frac{d}{\delta}\E[\ell(x+\delta S)\,S] = \nabla\E\,\ell(x+\delta B)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP17.8
nodes.statement: Verify the 1D case via the fundamental theorem of calculus, lift to $d$ dimensions using Lemma LP17.7 and the identity $\mathrm{Vol}(\Sphere) = d\,\mathrm{Vol}(\Ball)$.

nodes.name: Two-point loss vs.\ smoothed loss
nodes.statement: For $G$-Lipschitz convex differentiable $\ell_t$ and $x \in \cK \subseteq R\,\Ball$ with $\xi \in [0,1]$, $\frac{1}{2}\sum_t (\ell_t(X_t^+)+\ell_t(X_t^-)) - \sum_t \ell_t(x) \le \sum_t \tilde{\ell}_t(x_t) - \sum_t \tilde{\ell}_t((1-\xi)x) + 3\delta G n + \xi G R n$.
conclusions: The displayed inequality holds for all realizations of $(X_t^+,X_t^-)$

nodes.name: Proof of LP17.9
nodes.statement: Use Lipschitzness: $|\ell_t(x)-\tilde{\ell}_t(x)| \le \delta G$ and $|\tilde{\ell}_t((1-\xi)x)-\ell_t((1-\xi)x)| \le \delta G$; bound $\ell_t((1-\xi)x) - \ell_t(x)$ by $\xi G R$.

nodes.name: Regret of OSGD with two-point feedback
nodes.statement: On $\cK$ with $r\,\Ball \subseteq \cK \subseteq R\,\Ball$, OSGD on $(1-\delta/r)\cK$ with two-point estimate satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le R^2/\eta + \eta(Gd)^2 n + \delta(3+R/r)Gn$. With $\eta = R/(Gd\sqrt{n})$, $\delta\to 0$: $\overline{R}_n \le 2RGd\sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.22
nodes.statement: Verify the perturbed points stay in $\cK$ (using $r\,\Sphere \subseteq \cK$ and convexity); apply Lemma LP17.9 with $\xi = \delta/r$ and Theorem TP17.18 with $\tilde{x}_t = x_t$ on smoothed losses $\tilde{\ell}_t$; bound $\|\tilde{g}_t\| \le Gd$.

nodes.name: Regret of OSGD with one-point feedback
nodes.statement: OSGD on $(1-\delta/r)\cK$ with one-point estimate satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le R^2/\eta + ((dL)^2/\delta^2)\eta n + \delta(3+R/r)Gn$. With $\delta = (2n)^{-1/4}\sqrt{RdL/((3+R/r)G)}$ and $\eta = (2n)^{-3/4}\sqrt{R^3/(dL(3+R/r)G)}$, $\overline{R}_n \le 4n^{3/4}\sqrt{RdL(3+R/r)G}$.
assumptions: $G$-Lipschitz convex differentiable losses uniformly bounded by $L$

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.23
nodes.statement: Mirror the two-point proof using $\|\tilde{g}_t\| \le dL/\delta$ from $|\ell_t(x+\delta S)| \le L$.

nodes.name: Nonlinear stochastic bandit on $[0,1]$ (unimodal)
nodes.statement: Arms $x_t \in [0,1]$; play yields $Y_t \in [0,1]$ with $\E[Y_t \mid x_t] = \mu(x_t)$ for fixed unknown unimodal $\mu : [0,1]\to[0,1]$; goal: bound $\overline{R}_n = \sum_t \mu(x_t) - n\max_x \mu(x)$.

nodes.name: SGS (Stochastic Golden Search)
nodes.statement: Stochastic version of golden section search: at each stage, query four points (the current bracket and the new golden-ratio point) $\tfrac{2}{\epsilon_s^2}\ln(6n)$ times, eliminate one of the outer subintervals based on the empirical winner.

nodes.name: Two-sided strong-mode condition
nodes.statement: $\mu$ is unimodal on $[0,1]$ with mode $x^*$; there exists $C_L > 0$ such that $|\mu(x)-\mu(x')| \ge C_L|x-x'|$ for $x,x'$ both in $[0,x^*-1/C_L]$ or both in $[x^*+1/C_L,1]$. Additionally $\mu$ is $C_H$-Lipschitz.

nodes.name: SGS bracket retains $x^*$ with high probability
nodes.statement: If $\epsilon_s = C_L \varphi^{-(s+3)}$ then $\P(x^* \notin [x_{A,s},x_{C,s}]) \le s/n$ uniformly in $s \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP17.10
nodes.statement: Recursive decomposition; conditional probability of mistake bounded by Hoeffding union bound times $6\,e^{-T_s\Delta_s^2/8} \le 1/n$ using $\Delta_s \ge C_L\varphi^{-(s+3)} = \epsilon_s$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-regret of SGS
nodes.statement: For unimodal $C_H$-Lipschitz $\mu$ satisfying the strong-mode condition, SGS with $\epsilon_s = C_L\varphi^{-(s+3)}$ satisfies $\overline{R}_n \le \frac{C_H}{C_L^2}\,8\varphi^6\ln(6n)\bigl[\frac{2\varphi}{\varphi-1}\sqrt{1+C_L^2 n} + \frac{1}{4}\log_{\varphi}^2(1+C_L^2 n)\bigr]$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP17.24
nodes.statement: Decompose pseudo-regret per stage; bound each stage's regret using Lipschitz $\mu$, $|x_{C,s}-x_{A,s}|\le \varphi^{-s}$, and Lemma LP17.10; bound the number of stages by $S \le \frac{1}{2}\log_\varphi(1+C_L^2 n)$.

nodes.name: Stochastic vs.\ adversarial bandits (SAO)
nodes.statement: The SAO algorithm of Bubeck-Slivkins (2012) achieves $\overline{R}_n = \mathcal{O}(K\log^2(n)\log(K)/\Delta)$ in the stochastic regime and $\overline{R}_n = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{nK}\log^{3/2}(n)\log(K))$ in the adversarial regime simultaneously.

nodes.name: INF strategy attains $\sqrt{nK}$ regret
nodes.statement: The INF (Implicitly Normalized Forecaster) of Audibert-Bubeck (2009) closes the $\sqrt{\ln K}$ gap in adversarial bandit regret using $\psi(x) = (-\eta x)^{-q}$ with $q > 1$.

nodes.name: Optimal stochastic-bandit minimax-and-distribution-dependent strategy
nodes.statement: Find a strategy with regret always better than both MOSS and improved UCB; conjectured: $\sum_{i:\Delta_i>0}\frac{1}{\Delta_i}\ln(n/H)$ with $H = \sum_{i:\Delta_i>0}\Delta_i^{-2}$.
